subject: english
question:
Choose the correct meaning of idiom:

**Carry coals to Newcastle**

options.text: Provide something where it is already abundant

solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Provide something where it is already abundant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "**Carry coals to Newcastle**" means to do something that is redundant or unnecessary because the place already has an abundance of the thing being provided.
 
• Newcastle is a city in England that was historically known for its coal production. Hence, taking coal to Newcastle would be pointless as the city already had plenty of it.
 
• This idiom is often used to describe actions that are futile or excessive.

Correct interpretation: *"Provide something where it is already abundant."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other examples of idioms with similar usage:**
 
 
• "Preaching to the choir" - giving advice to people who already agree or understand.
 
• "Selling ice to Eskimos" - trying to sell something to people who don't need it.
 
 
 
• **Usage:** This idiom is used in situations where someone's efforts are unnecessary or duplicative.
